meta.title: Card payment with 3-D Secure
meta.description: An online card payment that the issuer challenges with 3-D Secure 2: who calls whom, from Pay now to the order confirmation.

summary.headline: The issuer decides whether to challenge; once the shopper passes, the authentication value travels with the authorisation so the issuer carries the fraud liability.
points: The merchant never sees the card number; it pays with a gateway token
Device data lets the issuer approve most payments without a challenge
The challenge runs between the browser and the issuer's access control server
Authorisation carries the CAVV, which shifts fraud liability to the issuer

data.title: Merchant backend
data.subtitle: Larkfield Outdoor shop
data.description: Creates the payment for the basket total, reacts to the gateway's next action and confirms the order once the payment succeeds.

data.title: Shopper's browser
data.subtitle: Checkout page
data.description: Card details go straight from hosted fields to the gateway, which hands back a token. The merchant's page never holds the card number.

data.title: Payment gateway
data.subtitle: Tollgate Payments
data.description: Runs the 3-D Secure server, routes the authorisation to the card scheme and reports one payment status back to the merchant.

data.title: Access control server
data.subtitle: Issuer's 3DS service
data.description: Scores the device and transaction data, then either approves frictionlessly or challenges the cardholder with a one-time code or banking app.

data.title: Issuing bank
data.subtitle: Authorisation host
data.description: Checks funds, card status and the authentication value, then approves or declines the authorisation.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: A shopper pays £86.40 for a tent. The issuer asks for a one-time code before it approves, so the payment takes a detour through 3-D Secure.

steps.title: The merchant creates the payment
steps.description: The browser sends the gateway token, never the card number. The merchant creates a payment for the basket total with an idempotency key, so a double click cannot charge twice.

steps.title: The issuer asks for a challenge
steps.description: The gateway's 3DS server sends the issuer's access control server the device data and transaction details. This one scores as unusual (new device, high basket), so the answer is a challenge, which the gateway passes back as requires_action.

steps.title: The shopper passes the challenge
steps.description: The checkout opens the issuer's challenge in a frame. The shopper types the code from a text message; the access control server checks it and returns an authentication value to the browser.

steps.title: Authorisation with the CAVV
steps.description: The access control server also sends the result to the gateway's 3DS server on the back channel. The gateway then sends the authorisation through the card scheme with the CAVV attached, and the issuer approves.

steps.title: The order is confirmed
steps.description: The gateway reports the payment as succeeded. The merchant marks the order paid and shows the confirmation page. Funds are captured later, when the tent ships.
